corrected_content.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th row:

$$
\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}.
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ {\color{red}3} & {\color{red}0} & {\color{red}0} & {\color{red}1}\end{vmatrix} & ={\color{red}3}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{41}}+{\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{42}}+{\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{43}}+{\color{red}1}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{44}} \\  & ={\color{red}3}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{4+1}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}2 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4\end{vmatrix}}+{\color{red}1}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{4+4}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{vmatrix}} \\  & =-3\begin{vmatrix}2 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{vmatrix}.\end{aligned}$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain: 

$$\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 4 & 1 \\ {\color{red}2} & {\color{red}0} & {\color{red}0} \\ 1 & -2 & 4\end{vmatrix} & ={\color{red}2}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{21}}+{\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{22}}+{\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{23}} \\  & ={\color{red}2}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{2+1}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}4 & 1 \\ -2 & 4\end{vmatrix}} \\  & =-2\begin{vmatrix}4 & 1 \\ -2 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-2(16-(-2)) \\  & =-36\end{aligned}$$

 
Finally, we compute the second $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along its $3$rd row:

$$\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ {\color{red}0} & {\color{red}1} & {\color{red}-2}\end{vmatrix} & ={\color{red}0}\cdot {\color{black}{C}_{31}}+{\color{red}1}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{32}}+{\color{red}(-2)}\cdot {\color{blue}{C}_{33}} \\  & ={\color{red}1}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{3+2}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix}}+{\color{red}(-2)}\cdot {\color{blue}(-1)^{3+3}\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}} \\  & =-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(0-4)-2(2-2) \\  & =4+0 \\  & =4\end{aligned}$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}=-3\cdot (-36)+1\cdot 4=112.
$$
